copy.heading: Choose how your agents think
copy.body: Sign in directly with the model provider. Use your normal subscription or API directly with the provider.
Ronin does not resell model access or place itself between you and the provider.

media.label: Install a provider
media.description: Choosing a provider in Setup, and what installation opens

copy.heading: Introduce yourself
copy.body: Registering gives you access to Ronin Services and lets you take part in the Bounty Program. Both are free.
It is not required. Ronin works without it, and Services already installed stay usable either way.

media.label: Registration and Services
media.description: What registering establishes, and what it does not gate

copy.heading: Choose a Workspace Folder
copy.body: Your project roots: directories on this machine and GitHub repositories. They give Agents known surfaces to work on.
Add the directory or repository you want worked on. Register more at any time.
Authenticate with GitHub to reach remote repositories too.
Give each Agent its own desk for code, or share one checkout for documents and plans.

media.label: Workspace Folders
media.description: What a Workspace Folder is, and how to choose one

copy.heading: Choose installations
copy.body: Optional facilities. The coworkspace stays local and light without any of them.
Skip anything you are unsure about; add it the day you need it.
The ones Ronin maintains ask you to register first. They are open code and free.
In return Ronin counts tool use — never your code, prompts or messages — and asks you not to commercialize the tools.

media.label: Ronin Services
media.description: Optional capabilities, and how to switch them on

copy.heading: Start one Agent
copy.body: Everything before this was setup. This is the part that does work.
Give the Agent one clear objective, small enough that you can check the result yourself.
Set its reach: discuss talks it through, plan plans, execute completes the agreed work.
